title: Rootless API service panics in vendored pgzip (slice bounds out of range) on gzipped tar PUT to /containers/{id}/archive; "ddev start" fails with EOF
body:
### Issue Description

The Podman API service panics and exits when a client uploads a gzipped tar that
ends right after the end-of-archive marker (what Go's `archive/tar` produces) to
`PUT /v1.44/containers/{id}/archive` of a running container. The client only sees
the connection closing:

```
Put "http://%2Frun%2Fuser%2F1000%2Fpodman%2Fpodman.sock/v1.44/containers/<id>/archive?path=%2Fmnt%2Fv%2Ftraefik": EOF
```

I hit this with DDEV 1.25.4: `ddev start` pushes the mkcert CA and the Traefik
config into volumes through this endpoint and fails with
`Failed to copy root CA into Docker volume ... EOF` followed by
`failed to push global Traefik config ... EOF`.

The panic is in the vendored `github.com/klauspost/pgzip` (v1.2.6), in
`Reader.WriteTo`. The root cause is a stale read offset in pgzip, reported here:
https://github.com/klauspost/pgzip/issues/74. pgzip v1.2.7 and master have the same bug, so the
dependency bump to v1.2.7 (#29864) will not fix it.

Not tested: Podman 5.x.

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1. Start any container: `podman run -d --name t docker.io/library/alpine:latest sleep 300`
2. Create a gzipped tar that ends right after the end-of-archive marker:
   `head -c 1500 /dev/urandom | base64 > a.txt`
   `tar -b 1 -cf x.tar a.txt && gzip -k x.tar` (GNU tar's default pads the archive
   to 10240 bytes and hides the bug)
3. Upload it to the API socket:
   ```
   curl --unix-socket $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/podman/podman.sock -X PUT \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/x-tar' -H 'Transfer-Encoding: chunked' \
     --data-binary @x.tar.gz 'http://d/v1.44/containers/t/archive?path=/tmp'
   ```

Result on my machine (unpatched v6.1.3 build), from an equivalent script that does
the above with generated random text, once with a tar padded to 10240 bytes and once
with a tar that ends at the end marker:

```
1 file,  padded to 10240 (GNU default)   tar= 10240 bytes  HTTP 200
1 file,  exact end (Go-like)             tar=  3584 bytes  HTTP 000
```

`000` means curl got no HTTP response because the service died (the panic is in
`journalctl --user -u podman.service`). The same happens without a `Content-Type`
header, which is what DDEV sends. curl's default `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`
does not trigger it, so pass the header explicitly. The same tar uploaded
uncompressed works.

### Describe the results you received

The API service panics, the connection is closed without a response, and
systemd restarts the service on the next connection. `journalctl --user -u
podman.service` shows:

```
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [6144:0]

goroutine 1766 [running, locked to thread]:
github.com/klauspost/pgzip.(*Reader).WriteTo(0x0?, {0x1f3dc80?, 0x307e440?})
        vendor/github.com/klauspost/pgzip/gunzip.go:516 +0x5ec
io.copyBuffer({0x1f3dc80, 0x307e440}, {0x73271c1cd5e8, 0x7a2b77c60c0}, {0x0, 0x0, 0x0})
        $GOROOT/src/io/io.go:411 +0x9d
io.Copy(...)
        $GOROOT/src/io/io.go:388
go.podman.io/buildah/copier.copierHandlerPut.func5()
        vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/copier/copier.go:2486 +0x51a
go.podman.io/buildah/copier.copierWithoutSubprocess({_, _}, {_, _}, {{0x1e2b39b, 0x3}, {0x1f2d4b0, 0x1}, {0x1f2d4b0, 0x1}, ...})
        vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/copier/copier.go:789 +0x6ee
go.podman.io/buildah/copier.copier({_, _}, {_, _}, {{0x1e2b39b, 0x3}, {0x1f2d4b0, 0x1}, {0x0, 0x0}, ...})
        vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/copier/copier.go:759 +0x2ee
go.podman.io/buildah/copier.Put({0x1f2d4b0?, 0x20000?}, {0x7a2b7b236a0?, 0x7a2b7e45f08?}, {{0x7a2b77138c0, 0x3, 0x4}, {0x7a2b7713920, 0x3, 0x4}, ...}, ...)
        vendor/go.podman.io/buildah/copier/copier.go:490 +0x172
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).copyFromArchive.func7.1()
        libpod/container_copy_common.go:226 +0xb8
go.podman.io/podman/v6/libpod.(*Container).joinMountAndExec.func1()
        libpod/container_copy_linux.go:77 +0x31f
```

(Paths shortened. Same trace with Go 1.26.8 and 1.27.1.)


### Describe the results you expected

HTTP 200 and the files extracted into the container, as with the padded or the
uncompressed archive.

### Podman in a container

No

### Privileged Or Rootless

Rootless

### Upstream Latest Release

Yes

### Additional environment details

- Podman 6.1.3 built from source (tag v6.1.3, commit 85b994955e). The binary behind `podman info` above carries the local pgzip patch described in "Analysis", hence the `-dirty` suffix. The crash was observed before the patch was applied, with Go 1.26.8 and Go 1.27.1, and is gone with it.
- TUXEDO OS (Ubuntu-based), rootless with pasta, systemd user socket activation (`podman.socket` / `podman.service`)
- Client: DDEV 1.25.4 (Go Docker client); also reproduced with plain curl as above

### Additional information

Any Go client that sends `archive/tar` output (no 10240-byte padding) gzipped to this
endpoint can trigger it.

### Analysis

`pgzip.Reader.Read` sets `z.current = nil` after draining a block without
resetting `z.roff`. `WriteTo` then evaluates `z.current[z.roff:]` on a nil slice
with a stale offset. The tar reader in the copier consumes a stream that ends
exactly at the end marker through `Read`, then the remainder is drained with
`io.Copy`, which calls `WriteTo`. With GNU-style padding some bytes are still
buffered, `z.current` is not nil, and nothing happens. (I did not trace this
sequence in Podman's code; it is the pattern that reproduces the same panic in the
pgzip test linked above, and it matches the observation that padded archives work.)

Details, a test and a one-line fix: https://github.com/klauspost/pgzip/issues/74

Workaround used until a fixed pgzip is vendored: a local patch to
`vendor/github.com/klauspost/pgzip/gunzip.go` that guards the slice in
`WriteTo`:

```diff
 func (z *Reader) WriteTo(w io.Writer) (n int64, err error) {
 	total := int64(0)
-	avail := z.current[z.roff:]
+	var avail []byte
+	if z.roff <= len(z.current) {
+		avail = z.current[z.roff:]
+	}
 	if len(avail) != 0 {
```

With it, the upload above returns 200 and `ddev start` works.
